title: Dawnstrap transition manual (short)
content:
Context:
A quick, compressed passdown for the Dawnstrap shift — meant to be read in <5 minutes. This is a living scratchpad: decisions, temporary mitigations, and heuristics we used overnight. Use at your discretion and add follow-ups in the linked artifacts.

Shift summary (what happened):
- 02:10 UTC: Spike in token-latency from hosted-api (route: /v1/generate) — p95 rose from ~120ms to ~850ms for ~12 minutes.
- 02:16 UTC: Automated fallback to smaller-quant model (redwood/ft-6b-q8) triggered successfully; errors stayed low.
- 03:05 UTC: Failed Nvidia driver upgrade on dedicated pool-3; kernel panic on 1/4 nodes. Node auto-eviction worked, but capacity shortfall caused throttling on high-throughput customers.
- 04:40 UTC: Incident escalated (INC-2198) after queued requests > 300 for 6m. Manual reroute to reserve pool performed. Everything steady after 05:10 UTC.

Active items to monitor now (top of stack):
1) Pool-3 nodes health (GPU hostd) — grafana dashboard: infra/pool3-nodes — check node-17 which flapped once.
2) Model fallback error logs — query: prod.logs | service:hosted-api level:error "kv-cache" between 02:00-06:00 UTC.
3) Queues > 200? Alert rule: queued_requests_count > 200 for 5m (severity: page).

Quick commands (most-used):
- Check pool nodes: ssh ops@node-17 or run: ./tools/infra node-status --pool pool-3
- Drain a node (safe): ./tools/infra drain-node node-17 --grace 300 - To revert routing rule (if fallback misfires): curl -XPOST https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/routes/reload -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_KEY"
- Force small-quant rollout: ./deploy model-variant --model redwood/ft-6b-q8 --policy immediate --target hosted-api
- Re-enable KV cache (if someone disabled): ./runtime-admin cache toggle --pool hosted --state on

Temporary mitigations applied (do not assume permanent):
- 02:20 UTC: Lowered default max-batch to 16 for hosted-api when p95 > 400ms (quick fix, will impact throughput but reduces tail latency).
- 03:30 UTC: Evicted node-17 and cordoned pool-3. Node will remain cordoned until driver upgrade validated.
- 03:45 UTC: Manual traffic split: 70% hosted-api -> ft-13b-q4, 30% -> ft-6b-q8 to keep customer p50 stable.

Why these choices? Brief rationale:
- Reducing max-batch reduces queuing jitter during resource starvation (observed during previous similar spikes).
- Keeping the smaller quant variant live prevents full fallback to CPU for certain customers, offering predictable latency at cost of quality.

Outstanding unknowns / follow-ups (please file and tag):
- Was the driver upgrade attempt part of a rolling job started at 02:00? (Related PR: PR-834). Confirm schedule and revert plan.
- Validate if KV-cache disable came from an automated script (search: slack thread #deploys around 01:45 UTC).
- Investigate memory pressure on node-19 — OOM kills happened once around 04:12 UTC but no clear culprit.

Notes to next person (concrete tasks):
- Check INC-2198 timeline and add notes to JIRA with any new logs.
- Re-run the driver upgrade in staging and only schedule for prod after 24-hour bake.
- If queues trend upward (>150) for 10m, re-enable burst-capacity (command: ./ops capacity-burst allow --pool hosted --minutes 15) and page oncall if capacity still insufficient.

Escalation & contact matrix (quick):
- Primary SRE on-call: Diego Alvarez (pager)
- Serving runtime lead: Maya Lin (DM on Slack)
- Infra hardware: Kenji Sato (call/DM)
- If customer impact > 10% tail latency for > 15m: page Eng Pager (policy: page after 3 missed SLAs)

Temporary runbook additions (write up later into product doc):
- Add short-circuit to routing for pool-degraded state: route-out pool-3 -> reserve-pool. Manual toggle: ./control route toggle --from pool-3 --to reserve
- Add an observable for driver-update concurrency: gauge(driver.update.in_progress)

Short log snippets to keep (paste these to JIRA):
- "2026-03-10T02:12:43Z hosted-api p95 latency 847ms, queued_requests 412, fallback_triggered=true"
- "2026-03-10T03:03:21Z infra node-17 kernel_panic reason: nvidia-driver-534.12 upgrade failed"

Scratch thoughts / heuristics (no action unless confirmed):
- We should consider conservative driver-update windows: 03:00-04:30 UTC currently noisy for some customers. Maybe switch to 06:00-08:00 UTC for pool-3.
- Auto-fallback policy might be too aggressive: consider increasing the trigger threshold from 300 queued to 500 queued for model fallback to avoid oscillation.

TODO (short list):
- [ ] Add playbook entry for 'driver upgrade rollback' with exact commands and expected time to recover. (owner: Kenji)
- [ ] Add unit/regression test around the KV-cache toggle to prevent accidental disablement during deployment. (owner: Asha)
- [ ] Create a small alert runbook for "queued requests > 200" to reduce noise and clarify paging thresholds. (owner: Diego)

Final quick handover note:
- Systems are stable now but watch the queue metric for the next 2 hours. If you see a slow upward trend, run the capacity-burst command before escalating. Leave notes here and ping Diego in #sre-shift-logs.

If anything is unclear: ping me (Asha) on Slack or leave a comment in the JIRA. I'm around until 12:30 UTC to assist with the driver re-test.

-- Asha
